report.summary: Audited visible portion of ledger.py. Critical: _terminal_event is truncated, causing SyntaxError/NameError on any call to mark_completed or mark_failed. Additionally, _row_to_intent is used but not defined in the provided excerpt; if missing, it crashes record_intent. Docstring claims resolve_by_effect exists but it is not visible, leaving crash-recovery handshake unverifiable. Remaining visible logic aligns with documented guarantees; no swallowed errors or concurrency defects seen.

risks.trigger: Any call to mark_completed or mark_failed -> _resolve -> _terminal_event returns a malformed SQL string, causing sqlite3.ProgrammingError.
record_intent (or any completion) returns Intent via _row_to_intent; if not defined later, NameError on first use.
Docstring describes resolve_by_effect as the handshake for crash recovery, but its implementation is not in the provided excerpt; absence would break the claimed recovery contract.

todos: Complete _terminal_event method with proper SQL and fetchone logic.
Define _row_to_intent or confirm its existence in the full file.
Verify resolve_by_effect, open_intents, and other missing methods exist and match docstring guarantees.
Add a test covering resolution attempt that triggers the incomplete code path to catch this earlier.

handoff.suggestion: Paste the full _terminal_event and any missing helper functions. Consider adding a smudge test that calls mark_completed on a fresh intent to immediately expose the syntax error.
